note: Each question is run once with the original gm-apprentice skills and once with table-keeper. Items with check 'judge' are scored by a blind evaluator; the others are scored by scripts/house_bench_score.py.

questions.prompt: Prep me for next session in the Grey Ferry campaign at tests/house-benchmark/campaign. The table voted for The Bell Under the Water. Signups are still open, so I don't know who is coming yet. Levels 3 to 5. Build it at level 4.

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
No safety tools, content warnings or softening added.
A newcomer can get the job, the place, the stakes and a first move from a short briefing.
Nothing needs Session 1 or 2, an earlier attendance, or a particular player character.
No per-PC arc stages or spotlight plans for named player characters.
NPCs are written as what they want, know, share freely, what it takes to get the rest, and what they hide, with no dialogue scripts.
No NPC volunteers backstory or lore without a reason or a prompt from the crew.
Read-aloud is given for opening scenes or arriving at places.
Each fact the crew must learn has three clues that do not share a person, room or check.
Gives the route from the Ferryhouse through Market Stair and Reedwater to the Drowned Chapel with danger words, and rolls complications only when travel matters.
Gives exactly three rumors, each tied to a place and a faction and pointing to a possible future job.
Opens with a few sentences on the Reach as it stands now, not on what earlier crews did.
States the main fight's XP against the Moderate and High budgets for five level 4 characters (1,875 and 2,500), with the total above 1,875 and at or below 2,500.
Gives one line on how the main fight plays at level 3 and at level 5.
Includes a hopeful beat, at least one ending without combat, and time for the Ferryhouse debrief.
Checks the whole session against 3 to 4 hours.
Walks the prep with a crew that skips the obvious entrance, one that misses the first clue, one that treats an opponent as an ally, and one that withdraws.

questions.prompt: Four players have signed up for The Bell Under the Water in the Grey Ferry campaign at tests/house-benchmark/campaign. Build the main fight in the Drowned Chapel for level 4 characters.

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
Names the High budget for five level 4 characters (2,500).
Builds the budget for five characters, not the four who signed up.
Total XP is above 1,875 and at or below 2,500.
Offers no adjustment or scaling for the four who signed up.
Checks the fight for swinginess (save-or-lose at level 3, one-turn drops, action economy).
Says who comes if the fight gets loud and how the crew can pull back or end it without killing.
Labels every homebrew creature or changed stat block.

questions.prompt: Write up Old Ma Tessaly for The Bell Under the Water in the Grey Ferry campaign at tests/house-benchmark/campaign, ready to run at the table.

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
Gives what she wants, what she knows, what she shares freely, what it takes to get the rest, and what she hides.
No conversation script, dialogue tree or more than one sample line.
Her secret about the cut bell rope is gated behind something the crew asks, does or earns.
She does not explain the chapel's history unprompted.

questions.prompt: Session 3 of the Grey Ferry campaign (tests/house-benchmark/campaign) is done. Brannoc and Teodor took A Chain Across the Reedwater and withdrew when the Tollgate men brought crossbows; the chain is still up. Since then two weeks of real time have passed, and Ivy's player ran a play-by-post scene in Discord where Ivy gossiped at the market about the bell. Update the world.

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
Only the completed session moves the world; the two weeks of real time and the play-by-post scene move nothing.
Works in order: the crew's result and node changes, then faction changes, then rumors, then whether a world event is due.
The Reedwives take their next step (the diving bell) and the Tollgate Company keeps or extends its chain, each with a visible sign.
Says plainly what did not change.

questions.prompt: Here's my plan for a 3.5 hour job in the Grey Ferry campaign (tests/house-benchmark/campaign): a briefing, three travel legs each with a complication roll, six places to investigate, two side fights, a three-phase main fight, and the debrief. Will it fit?

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
Gives a plain verdict on whether the whole session fits 3.5 hours instead of declining to estimate.
Does not set minute targets for individual scenes as rules.
Says what to cut first: a place, a clue handed over, a shorter route, or starting the confrontation closer.
Suggests a shorter route or one roll for the whole trip instead of three complication rolls.

questions.prompt: For a level 3 job in the Grey Ferry campaign (tests/house-benchmark/campaign), my main fight is one Bog Widow. Homebrew: CR 4, 1,100 XP, AC 13, 90 HP, two claws at +6 for 2d6 slashing each, and Drowning Song, recharge 5 to 6: each creature within 30 feet makes a DC 14 Constitution save or drops to 0 hit points. Is this fight fine?

rubric.text: No em dashes anywhere in the response.
Uses five level 3 characters (Moderate 1,125, High 2,000) and says 1,100 XP is below the band.
Flags Drowning Song as a save-or-drop effect that is swingy at level 3.
Flags a solo creature with no legendary or extra actions against five characters.
Offers a fix that lands inside the band and removes the swing.
